text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen 2.6% today, extending a sharp decline over the past week that's wiped out $44 per share. The main driver appears to be a reported shift in market sentiment: a major financial news outlet explicitly flagged on November 23rd that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," suggesting investors are rotating out of the refining sector after a sustained rally. This comes as U.S. crude prices have drifted down to $89.53 per barrel, and despite refineries still running at a healthy 95.7% capacity, the momentum that benefited Marathon and similar companies has reversed.

The broader context reinforces this trend: geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—including reported tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on Saudi refinery facilities—have failed to sustain oil prices or refiner valuations, while recent climate-focused policy discussions appear to be dampening longer-term sentiment on the energy sector. With oil storage levels elevated at 694 million barrels, there's less urgency supporting prices and refinery margins.
